sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and file location
sections.what: Loads the compatibility helper and the recommended ESLint rules, and works out the folder this file lives in.
sections.why: Needed so shared rules can be found from any folder in the repo.

sections.name: compat
sections.title: Shared rules loader
sections.what: Creates the helper that lets the older shared rule file be used in this newer setup format.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared rules were written in the older format.
sections.watch_out: The base path is relative, and whether it resolves correctly has not been verified here.

sections.name: default export
sections.title: Skipped folders and project rules
sections.what: Lists folders to ignore, including services and generated code. Then loads the shared rules and sets rules for import order, unused variables, any-type use and console messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: the services folder is checked by other tools, and generated files should not be checked.
sections.watch_out: Ignoring the services folder means Python issues are never reported by this file.

summary: Sets the code rules ESLint uses for the JavaScript and TypeScript code in the monorepo, and skips Python and other folders.
purpose: Keeps the code consistent and catches common mistakes such as unused variables and disordered imports.
why: Likely reason: one shared check keeps every app consistent. The reason for skipping some folders is not stated in the code.
how: Sets a list of folders to skip, loads the shared base rules, then changes some rules to warnings.
inputs: The shared base rules file in packages/eslint-config and the source files in the repo.
outputs: Warnings or errors shown when lint runs.
risks: Several rules are only warnings, so they do not fail the build. The shared base file is loaded through a relative path that may not resolve as intended. Python code is not checked by this file.
debug: Run the lint command and read the rule name in each message. If rules seem missing, check the shared base path.
